content.jointProblem: Can site-specific statistical or one-class models detect meaningful deviations in ProtoSense's Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic without labelled attacks for training, while producing understandable alerts within appliance resource limits? The first experiment would test transfer to BACnet and ArmaturaSec's hardware using time-separated client captures and controlled bench anomalies, measuring operational alert burden, detection of injected scenarios, explanation usefulness, and resource consumption rather than assuming published results will transfer.

rationale.text: Kiss has directly relevant experience developing and calibrating unsupervised detectors without labelled attack data on operational SCADA networks.

sources.quote: The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data
enabling validation under real traffic conditions.

rationale.text: Her Modbus research provides a concrete starting point for site-specific baselines based on register timing, values, and command sequences.

sources.quote: For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated

rationale.text: Her work addresses adaptation to legitimate process changes, including an operator-acknowledged reset rather than relying solely on automatic baseline updates.

sources.quote: Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested.

rationale.text: She has measured resource-efficient inference on an embedded ARM target, providing relevant deployment experience, though not validation on ArmaturaSec's appliances.

sources.quote: A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: Her group has infrastructure for controlled ICS experiments and reproducible Modbus attack evaluation.

sources.quote: The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
The paper documents the testbed topology, PLC configuration, traffic generation scripts, and labelling methodology in sufficient detail for reproduction.

rationale.text: A joint project matches her stated preference for deployment-oriented industrial collaboration.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments.

constraints.text: Training and operational threshold selection must not depend on confirmed malicious client captures; archives must be treated as potentially contaminated rather than certified clean.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic
A few of them have been running their networks for twenty years with no security monitoring at all, so if they were compromised they would not know.

constraints.text: The solution must cover both Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP, learn site-specific normal behaviour, and control operational false alarms rather than relying on public-dataset performance.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site
it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.

constraints.text: Inference must run on-device within measured resource and packet-forwarding budgets, with integration into the existing embedded firmware environment.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device
support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.
Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
C and Rust for firmware components

constraints.text: Alerts must support explanations understandable to a plant manager; explanation usefulness needs explicit user evaluation.

sources.quote: We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Scope must fit one to two part-time company engineers, with archive, bench, and firmware access governed by an NDA.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.

constraints.text: Use of the research group's testbed requires a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

risks: The supplied research demonstrates Modbus and other ICS protocols, but not BACnet-specific validation. BACnet feature semantics, normal operating modes, and controlled anomalies must be tested in the first experiment.

Historical client traffic may contain unnoticed compromise or omit rare legitimate operating modes. A learned baseline could normalise malicious activity or generate nuisance alerts during maintenance and seasonal changes.

Injected bench attacks cannot establish real-world attack recall. The company's prior failure with public ICS data makes deployment transfer a central uncertainty; operational alerts will require expert adjudication.
Automatic adaptation could absorb persistent malicious behaviour, while restrictive updates could cause alert storms after legitimate reconfiguration.
Published ARM measurements do not establish compatibility with the current ProtoSense appliance. The planned late-2025 hardware variant's actual availability and specifications are unknown.
Statistical deviations may be explainable as changed timing or register behaviour without proving malicious intent. Plant-manager comprehension has not been demonstrated in the supplied evidence.
Researcher availability, project budget, delivery schedule, and client permissions for research use or transfer of captures remain unknown; these could prevent execution despite open participation.
questions: What time can Kiss and her group commit, who would implement the prototype, and what budget, milestones, and delivery deadline can both parties support?
Which appliance will host the pilot, is the planned hardware variant available, and what are its CPU, RAM, storage, throughput, and allowable inference and forwarding-latency budgets?
Do client agreements permit research access and bench replay of captures? What anonymisation, storage location, retention, publication, and IP terms must the NDA and data-sharing agreement cover?
How much traffic is available per site and protocol, and are maintenance, process changes, operating modes, outages, and existing security findings documented?

Can the first experiment include BACnet-capable devices or simulators and representative controlled anomalies, alongside time-separated Modbus and BACnet archive replay, without injecting attacks into live plants?
What alert burden per site and detection delay are acceptable, who will adjudicate pilot alerts, and which controlled scenarios define initial acceptance criteria?
Which plain-language alert explanations would plant managers find actionable, and can representative users participate in evaluating them?
Who may approve baseline updates or resets, and how should the detector distinguish planned reconfiguration from suspicious persistent changes?
